# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 70 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 48 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_070_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 70

**1** Jesus said: "If you bring forth what is within you, what you bring forth will save you.

**2** If you do not bring forth what is within you, what you do not bring forth will kill you."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"Bring forth"** — the standard rendering of the Coptic action verb here; PNEUMA's "give birth to" is a vivid metaphorical expansion that is not linguistically required.

**"Kill you"** — EMET preferred over "destroy you" (LOGOS): the Coptic uses the straightforward death verb (*mou*), not a destruction metaphor.

**Theological Note:** The symmetry of the structure is the theological point: the same inner reality is savior or killer depending on whether it is expressed or suppressed. This saying has been cited as a parallel to Jung's concept of the shadow, though the Thomasine context is specifically about spiritual self-realization.

**Synoptic Parallels:** No direct Synoptic parallel. The saying is unique to Thomas and stands as one of the most frequently quoted passages from the collection.
